chapter: Other pianists and the New Orleans scene
title: Piron's society orchestra and its pianists
summary: She heard Piron's society band and met it at carnival balls and the country club. She names its pianists. Everyone she played with read music.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Did you hear much of Pierron's orchestra when you were young?

Yes, when I faced young, the orchestra, Pierron's orchestra was a society band here. They were very good, I heard them. And then after we organized a large band, we would meet them playing the different balls, because at that time we were playing the carnival balls. And Pierron's band and our band would be the bands of the night. And at the country club we would meet them quite often.
So they had quite a nice band?
Yes, it was a lovely, real society band.
Who was playing piano with them at that time?
Um, Alagretta Alexander, when I heard them, the first time I heard them was The Pianist Who's Dead Now. Maybe you know his name, Mr. Russell.
Steve Lewis, the first one whom I heard once or twice, but he died shortly after. And then Alexander, Alagretta Alexander was a pianist most of the time after that.
Did most of the piano players around here, I mean, obviously they didn't play on the same style, but did they mostly play the same parts in a band?
Yes, when they were reading they had to play the same part, because everybody would improvise differently, I should imagine.
So most of the musicians that you came in contact with were reading musicians, really?
Yes, those with whom I played were all reading musicians. I haven't been with anyone other than reading musicians since I've been a musician.
